concepts.def: The repeating pattern in physical and chemical properties of elements across each period, caused by recurring outer electron configurations.
Reactivity with water increases down Group 2 because ionisation energies decrease, so the two outer electrons are lost more easily.
Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group, so barium hydroxide is far more soluble than magnesium hydroxide.
Oxidising ability decreases down Group 7, so chlorine displaces bromide and iodide ions from solution but iodine displaces neither.
Reducing ability of halide ions increases down the group as the ions get larger and lose an electron more easily.
A redox reaction in which the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced, as when chlorine reacts with cold dilute sodium hydroxide.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Group 2 hydroxide is least soluble in water?
options: Mg(OH)₂
Ca(OH)₂
Sr(OH)₂
Ba(OH)₂

mcqs.q: Which halogen will displace bromide ions from aqueous solution?
options: Chlorine
Iodine
Bromine
None of these

mcqs.q: When chlorine reacts with cold dilute NaOH, the chlorine is:
options: Simultaneously oxidised and reduced
Only oxidised
Only reduced
Neither oxidised nor reduced

mcqs.q: Which halide ion is the strongest reducing agent?
options: I⁻
F⁻
Cl⁻
Br⁻

mcqs.q: Why does reactivity increase down Group 2?
options: Reactivity increases because the atoms have more electrons to give away.
Atomic radius increases and ionisation energies decrease, so the two outer electrons are lost more easily.
Chlorine is stronger only because it is a gas at room temperature.
Reactivity increases because the nuclear charge decreases down the group.

mcqs.q: Why is chlorine a stronger oxidising agent than iodine?
options: Chlorine is stronger only because it is a gas at room temperature.
Chlorine atoms are smaller, so the incoming electron is closer to the nucleus, less shielded, and gained more readily.
Iodine is the stronger oxidising agent because it is bigger and has more electrons.
Reactivity increases because the nuclear charge decreases down the group.

mcqs.q: Can silver nitrate solution distinguish between halide ions?
options: All silver halide precipitates look identical, so silver nitrate cannot tell halides apart.
Silver nitrate turns each halide solution a different shade of blue.
Reactivity increases because the nuclear charge decreases down the group.
Yes — AgCl is white, AgBr cream and AgI yellow, and their different solubilities in ammonia confirm the identification.
